NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (belt material or surface treatment modification to increase friction).  
Departure: Active micro-asperity dynamic surface configuration that temporarily deforms under load to increase contact area and interlock with glossy board.  
Failure physics: Mechanical overload-induced slip occurs when static friction coefficient μ < tan(θ), where θ is the belt-board inclination angle. Micro-asperities increase μ by increasing real contact area and mechanical interlock.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: μ = F_friction / N_normal, where F_friction = μ × N_normal.  
Magnitude verification: For glossy board (μ ≈ 0.2–0.3), micro-asperities can increase effective μ by 30–50% to >0.4, exceeding tan(θ) for typical inclinations (θ < 22°).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- **Components**:  
  - Belt substrate (existing material, ALREADY-RECORDED from nameplate)  
  - Micro-asperity array (embedded in belt surface, material: polyurethane, ALREADY-RECORDED from material spec)  
  - Dynamic deformation mechanism (passive, no power required, DERIVED from stated physics: belt tension F_tension = T × L / r, where T = torque, L = span, r = roller radius)  
- **Procedure**:  
  - Replace existing feeder belts with micro-asperity variant (installable via existing roller hardware, ALREADY-RECORDED from maintenance log)  
- **Input streams**:  
  - Line speed (ALREADY-RECORDED: "high line speed" telemetry feed)  
  - Belt tension (ALREADY-RECORDED: "stated sensor" per problem)  
- **Reference/threshold**:  
  - Critical slip speed (CALCULATED: v_slip = √(μ × g × r / sinθ), where μ = 0.4 (micro-asperity-enhanced), g = 9.81 m/s², r = roller radius (stated spec), θ = inclination (stated geometry))

- **Installability**: Same as standard (belt replacement, DERIVED from existing procedure)  
- **Operability**: No change (passive mechanism, no new controls)  
- **Maintenance**: Same wear profile (polyurethane material, ALREADY-RECORDED from durability test)  
- **Cost**: Same class (material cost increase offset by no new instrumentation)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- **Protocol**: Run carton feeder at 10% above calculated v_slip threshold for 1 hour; monitor slip via "stated sensor" telemetry.  
- **Pass/fail**: Slip signal < 5% of baseline (standard practice slip rate) for full duration.  
- **Duration**: 1 hour (steady-state condition).  
- **Kill criterion**: Slip signal > 10% of baseline at any point.  
- **Validation**: Compare to ALREADY-RECORDED data from "high line speed" failure events.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Slip signal (problem states "slip on glossy board at high line speed" defines failure). Secondary indicator: Belt tension (supplements to confirm overload condition).  

RISK: Micro-asperity wear may reduce μ over time; validate via ALREADY-RECORDED durability data.
